test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Machinist) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: A 100 mm point punch may have a body diameter of 10 mm and a 6 mm diameter point ground at an angle of ______.
solution:
**Concept**

 
• Punches are hand tools used in workshops to mark permanent locations or to create indentations for drilling and layout.
 
• A **Prick Punch** (often referred to as a point punch in specific contexts) is used for layout work.
 
• The point angle of the punch determines its specific application.
 
• Standard angles for prick punches are 30^circ or 60^circ, while a center punch typically has an angle of 90^circ.

**Explanation**

The prick punch or point punch is used for marking positions on metal surfaces. The specific choice of the point angle depends on the task:

 
• **30° Point Angle:** This sharp angle is used for making very small, accurate indentations that serve as pivot points for the legs of dividers during layout work.
 
• **60° Point Angle:** This angle is generally used for marking the position of layout lines more clearly.
 
• **90° Point Angle:** This is characteristic of a Center Punch, used to make a wide indentation to guide a drill bit.

According to standard engineering workshop specifications, a 100 mm length punch with a 10 mm body diameter and a 6 mm diameter point is a standard configuration for a prick punch ground at a 30^circ angle.

**Hence, the point of the punch is ground at an angle of **30^circ**.**</p
